# Internet Connectivity Monitor

A self-contained, single-page web app that continuously monitors your internet connectivity by pinging popular public URLs every 4 minutes.

**This project was created entirely with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/claude-code) — every line of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript was generated by AI.**

## Why?

Spectrum internet in Brooklyn, NY has frequent outages. I got tired of not knowing when the connection dropped or came back, so I built this monitor to keep a running log of connectivity events. Now I have proof when the internet goes down — and I know the moment it comes back.

## Features

- **Real-time status indicator** — large green/red dot showing online/offline status
- **Automatic checks every 4 minutes** — pings favicons from Google, Cloudflare, Amazon, Apple, and a large JSON API endpoint
- **Per-URL breakdown** — collapsible panel showing each endpoint's reachability and response time
- **Event history log** — timestamped record of connectivity changes, persisted to localStorage
- **Reconnection alerts** — browser notification and audio chime when the connection is restored
- **Light/dark mode** — toggle with preference saved across sessions
- **No dependencies** — single HTML file, no build tools, no server, no frameworks

## Usage

Open `index.html` in any browser. That's it.

Or visit the live version: [jamilnyc.github.io/internet-monitor](https://jamilnyc.github.io/internet-monitor/)

## How It Works

The page uses `fetch()` in `no-cors` mode to request small resources (favicons) from highly available public sites. If any request succeeds, you're online. If all fail, you're offline. Results are logged with timestamps and persisted to `localStorage` so history survives page refreshes.
